{"id": "169066b2-3916-43ff-8b1e-7bc750cde9dc", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_hOKCBxQQwPnxRLy14WU0Hn", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"API keys\",\"context\":\"## Generate a long-term API key\\n\\n**Warning:**\\n\\nLong-term keys are for exploration only. For production, use short-term keys. For more information, see Alternatives to long-term access keys.\\n\\nChoose the tab for your preferred method, and then follow the steps:\\n\\n#### Using Console\\n\\n1. Sign in to the AWS Management Console with an IAM identity that has permissions to use the Amazon Bedrock console. Then, open the Amazon Bedrock console at\\n <https://console.aws.amazon.com/bedrock>.\\n2. In the left navigation pane, select **API keys**.\\n3. In the **Long-term API keys** tab, choose **Generate long-term API keys**.\\n4. Choose an expiration time and optionally add permissions in **Advanced permissions**.\\n5. Choose **Generate**.\\n\\n#### Using CLI\\n\\n```\\n# Create an IAM user\\naws iam create-user --user-name bedrock-api-user\\n\\n# Attach permissions\\naws iam attach-user-policy --user-name bedrock-api-user \\\\\\n --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonBedrockLimitedAccess\\n\\n# Generate the API key (replace NUMBER-OF-DAYS)\\naws iam create-service-specific-credential \\\\\\n --user-name bedrock-api-user \\\\\\n --service-name bedrock.amazonaws.com \\\\\\n --credential-age-days ${NUMBER-OF-DAYS}\\n```\\n\\nThe `ServiceApiKeyValue` in the response is your API key.\\n\\nTo deactivate or delete the key later, use the `ServiceSpecificCredentialId` from the response:\\n\\n```\\n# Deactivate the key\\naws iam update-service-specific-credential \\\\\\n --user-name bedrock-api-user \\\\\\n --service-specific-credential-id ${ServiceSpecificCredentialId} \\\\\\n --status Inactive\\n\\n# Delete the key permanently\\naws iam delete-service-specific-credential \\\\\\n --user-name bedrock-api-user \\\\\\n --service-specific-credential-id ${ServiceSpecificCredentialId}\\n```\\n\\n#### Using Python\\n\\n```\\nimport boto3\\n\\niam_client = boto3.client(\\\"iam\\\")\\n\\n# Create IAM user\\niam_client.create_user(UserName=\\\"bedrock-api-user\\\")\\n\\n# Attach permissions\\niam_client.attach_user_policy(\\n UserName=\\\"bedrock-api-user\\\",\\n PolicyArn=\\\"arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonBedrockLimitedAccess\\\"\\n)\\n\\n# Generate API key\\nresponse = iam_client.create_service_specific_credential(\\n UserName=\\\"bedrock-api-user\\\",\\n ServiceName=\\\"bedrock\\n\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Handle compromised long-term and short-term Amazon Bedrock API keys\",\"context\":\"# Handle compromised long-term and short-term Amazon Bedrock API keys\\n\\nIf your API key becomes compromised, you should revoke permissions to use it. There are various methods that you can use to revoke permissions for an Amazon Bedrock API key:\\n\\n* For long-term Amazon Bedrock API keys, you can use the UpdateServiceSpecificCredential, ResetServiceSpecificCredential, or DeleteServiceSpecificCredential to revoke permissions in the following ways:\\n\\n + Set the status of the key to inactive. You can reactivate the key later.\\n + Reset the key. This action generates a new password for the key.\\n + Delete the key permanently.\\n\\n **Note:**\\n\\n To carry out these actions through the API, you must authenticate with AWS credentials and not with an Amazon Bedrock API key.\\n* For both long-term and short-term Amazon Bedrock API keys, you can attach IAM policies to revoke permissions.\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\nYou can't deactivate, reset, or delete an individual short-term Amazon Bedrock API key. The Amazon Bedrock console doesn't list short-term keys after you generate them or provide revocation actions for them. A short-term key is a pre-signed URL that inherits the credentials and expiration of the session that generated it. To prevent use before the key expires, see Invalidate an IAM session or Deny an identity the ability to make calls with an Amazon Bedrock API key. These controls affect the generating session or identity, not only one short-term key.\\n\\n###### Topics\\n\\n* Change the status of a long-term Amazon Bedrock API key\\n* Reset a long-term Amazon Bedrock API key\\n* Delete a long-term Amazon Bedrock API key\\n* Attach IAM policies to remove permissions for using an Amazon Bedrock API key\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys-revoke.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"How Amazon Bedrock API keys work\",\"context\":\"# How Amazon Bedrock API keys work\\n\\nThe following image compares the default process to get credentials to the use of the Amazon Bedrock API key:\\n\\nThe leftmost flow in the diagram shows the default process of creating an identity in either AWS IAM Identity Center or IAM. With this process, you attach IAM policies to that identity to provide permissions to perform API operations and then generate general AWS credentials for that identity. You can then use the credentials to make API calls in AWS.\\n\\nThe blue nodes indicate two more flows to authenticate specifically to Amazon Bedrock. Both flows involve creating an Amazon Bedrock API key with which you can authenticate to using Amazon Bedrock actions. You can generate the following types of keys:\\n\\n* **Short-term key** \u2013 A secure option that allows temporary access to using Amazon Bedrock.\\n\\n Short term keys have the following properties:\\n\\n + Valid for the shorter of the following values:\\n\\n - 12 hours\\n - The duration of the session generated by the IAM principal used to generate the key.\\n + Inherit the permissions attached to the principal used to generate the key.\\n + Can be used only in the AWS Region from which you generated it.\\n* **Long-term key** \u2013 Recommended only for exploration of Amazon Bedrock. You can set the time after which the key expires. When you generate a long-term key, it underlyingly creates an IAM user that's for you, attaches the IAM policies that you select, and associates the key with the user. After you generate the key, you can use the IAM service to modify permissions for the IAM user.\\n\\n **Warning:**\\n\\n We strongly recommend restricting the use of Amazon Bedrock API keys for exploration of Amazon Bedrock. When you're ready to incorporate Amazon Bedrock into applications with greater security requirements, you should switch to short-term credentials. For more information, see Alternatives to long-term access keys in the IAM User Guide\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys-how.html\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"API keys for Amazon Bedrock\",\"context\":\"# API keys for Amazon Bedrock\\n\\nAPI keys for Amazon Bedrock allow you to make programmatic API requests and integrate\\nwith\\nyour preferred library. You can have up to two long-term API keys (active, inactive,\\nor\\nexpired) at a time for each IAM user\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/help-panel/IAM/latest/console/hp_user_security_credentials_bedrock_api_keys.html\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"Control permissions for generating and using Amazon Bedrock API keys\",\"context\":\"### Prevent an identity from generating long-term keys and from using Amazon Bedrock API keys\\n\\nTo prevent an IAM identity from generating long-term Amazon Bedrock API keys and using any Amazon Bedrock API keys, attach the following policy to the identity:\\n\\n#### Using JSON\\n\\n#### Using\\n\\n```\\n{\\n \\\"Version\\\":\\\"2012-10-17\\\",\\n \\\"Statement\\\": [\\n {\\n \\\"Sid\\\":\\\"DenyBedrockShortAndLongTermAPIKeys\\\",\\n \\\"Effect\\\": \\\"Deny\\\",\\n \\\"Action\\\": [\\n \\\"iam:CreateServiceSpecificCredential\\\",\\n \\\"bedrock:CallWithBearerToken\\\",\\n \\\"bedrock-mantle:CallWithBearerToken\\\"\\n ],\\n \\\"Resource\\\": [\\n \\\"*\\\"\\n ]\\n }\\n ]\\n}\\n\\n```\\n\\nWarning\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\n* You can't prevent the generation of short-term keys.\\n* This policy will prevent the creation of credentials for all AWS services that support creating service-specific credentials. For more information, see Service-specific credentials for IAM users\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys-permissions.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Check Bedrock API key docs"}
